To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) QCD corrections to top quark pair production in $e^+e^-$ annihilation above threshold are large, (2) the QCD corrected top quark mass is larger than the pole mass by about 5%, (3) QCD corrections affect the angular distribution of the decay products of top quarks, (4) there is an ambiguity when reconstructing events that includes real gluons.

the QCD corrections increase the cross section by a factor of 1.4, the top quark polarization is significantly affected by the QCD corrections, and the top quark width is increased by a factor of $\ensuremath{\sim}1.4$.
the top mass and the helicity angle distributions are modified by the QCD corrections and that the ambiguities introduced by the QCD radiation are not important.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the production of a top quark-antiquark pair, ${e}^{±} {e}^{±}\ensuremath{\rightarrow}{t}\overline{t}$, in electron-positron collisions, where the top quark is assumed to decay promptly to a $W$-boson and a bottom quark.
the production and decay of top quarks in $e^+e^-$ collisions at next-to-leading-order (NLO) QCD.
the production of top quarks at the future linear $e^{+}e^{-}$ collider.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the QCD corrections are large, and the ambiguity in event reconstruction is significant.
the QCD corrections to top production and decay are small, but that the corrections to top decay are larger than the corrections to top production.
the $O({\alpha }_{s})$ QCD corrections are not large enough to change the conclusions drawn at the tree level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the QCD corrections increase the total rate by about 30% and the top quark decay rate by about 20% with a small change in the helicity angle distributions.
the $O({\alpha}_{s})$ corrections to $e^+e^-\to t\overline{ t}X$ are large, and that the $O(\alpha_{s}^{2})$ effects are not yet well understood.
the QCD corrections to ${e}^{+\ensuremath{-}}t\overline{\ensuremath{t}}$ are small and that the top quark is predominantly produced in the $s$-channel.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the QCD corrections to top quark production and decays are important for a precision measurement of the top quark properties.
the QCD corrections to top quark production and decays are not negligible and should be included in a realistic analysis.
the QCD corrections are large and positive and should be included in any precision analysis.
